title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00612
what_is_it: FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification reporting a UFO/UAP sighting by a commercial air transport crew.
core_summary: On February 19, 2024, the crew of Air Transport 3498, a Boeing 767-300 flying from Sacramento to Chicago-Rockford, reported seeing multiple lights moving and circling at or above flight level 370 (approximately 37,000 feet). The pilot first observed the UAP 20 nautical miles east-northeast of Mauston VOR (MTU). The objects were not detected on ATC facility radar.
interpretation_warnings: Single-source report from one flight crew with no corroborating radar data.

Coordinates in the metadata (near Rockford, IL) do not match the reported sighting location 20 NM ENE of MTU (Mauston, WI), suggesting coordinates may refer to the aircraft destination rather than sighting location.
No description of UAP shape, size, or behavior beyond 'lights moving and circling' — limited observational detail.
This is a preliminary notification, not a full investigation report.

public_headline: Airline Crew Reports Multiple Lights Circling at 37,000 Feet Over Wisconsin
public_tldr: An FAA incident notification records that the crew of a Boeing 767-300 cargo flight from Sacramento to Chicago-Rockford saw multiple lights moving and circling at or above 37,000 feet near Mauston, Wisconsin, on February 19, 2024. Air traffic control radar did not detect the objects.
public_narrative:
This document is an FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification — a preliminary report filed when something unusual is reported in US airspace. It is not a full investigation or a final conclusion. It records a single sighting by one flight crew.

On February 19, 2024, at 4:50 AM Central time, the crew of Air Transport 3498 — a Boeing 767-300 flying from Sacramento (SMF) to Chicago-Rockford (RFD) — reported seeing multiple lights moving and circling at or above flight level 370, roughly 37,000 feet. The pilot first observed the lights approximately 20 nautical miles east-northeast of the Mauston VOR navigation point in Wisconsin. Salt Lake City Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC) relayed the report.

Notably, the objects were not detected on air traffic control radar. The document provides no description of the lights beyond their movement pattern — no shape, size, colour, or speed is recorded.

The FAA filed this as a UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena) notification. There is no indication in the document of any follow-up investigation, explanation, or conclusion about what the crew observed.
public_caveats: This is a single-source report from one flight crew. No other aircraft or ground observers are recorded as corroborating the sighting.
The objects did not appear on ATC radar, which means there is no independent sensor data backing the visual observation.
The document is a preliminary notification, not a completed investigation. No cause or explanation is offered.
Very limited detail is provided about the lights — only that they were 'moving and circling.' No shape, size, or behaviour beyond that is described.
The coordinates in the document metadata appear to refer to the aircraft's destination (Rockford, IL), not the sighting location (near Mauston, WI). Readers should not confuse the two.
